concepts.title: Matter Is Made of Particles and Atoms

questions.q: What is matter made of according to modern science?
questions.a: Tiny particles - atoms and molecules - that are always moving and attract each other.

questions.q: What evidence shows matter is particulate?
questions.a: Dissolving, diffusion (spread of smell) and mixing of liquids show particles moving and fitting into gaps.

questions.q: Why can't a solid be compressed much?
questions.a: Its particles are packed tightly with very little space between them.

concepts.title: Subatomic Particles: Electron, Proton and Neutron

questions.q: Name the three subatomic particles with their charges.
Where are protons and neutrons located?
questions.a: In the tiny dense nucleus at the centre of the atom.

questions.q: What is the charge on an atom's electron and where does it move?
questions.a: Negative charge; electrons revolve in shells around the nucleus.

concepts.title: Atomic Models: From Thomson to Rutherford

questions.q: What did Rutherford's gold foil experiment reveal?
questions.a: Most alpha particles passed straight through (atom mostly empty) but a few bounced back (tiny dense positive nucleus).

questions.q: Why did Thomson's 'plum pudding' model fail?
questions.a: It could not explain alpha particles bouncing back from a concentrated positive centre.

questions.q: What model replaced Rutherford's to fix electron stability?
questions.a: Bohr's model - electrons occupy fixed energy shells and do not radiate energy inside them.
